summary: The Master of Science (M.Sc.) program in Food Science and Technology prepares students to make food production processes more sustainable, close cycles, and integrate alternative raw material sources into diets for a healthier, more sustainable, and varied food supply.

Official name: Biotechnology
Degree: Master of Science (M.Sc.)

This interdisciplinary, research-oriented program covers the properties, production processes, and applications of enzymes and microorganisms in the food, pharmaceutical, and chemical industries. Students gain expertise in biochemical methods, molecular biology, enzyme kinetics, mutagenesis, and handling food pathogens using modern laboratories and pilot plants.

The Master’s in Food Technology at Wageningen University & Research covers the science behind food production, processes, and innovation. Students acquire technological knowledge and practical skills to analyze food, solve technological problems, and develop innovative, sustainable food products through courses, a thesis, and an internship.

Wageningen University & Research offers a full-time, two-year English-taught Master's in Food Safety (MSc). The programme covers technical and legal aspects of food safety, food quality interaction, food safety management systems, and specialized tracks in Applied Food Safety, Food Law, and Supply Chain Safety.

The Department of Food Science offers course-based and research-based graduate programs, including the MSc in Food Safety and Quality Assurance, MSc in Food Science, and PhD in Food Science, focusing on food safety, preservation, dairy science, functional foods, and innovative sustainable food development.

Master of Science in Food Science (MSc) covers advanced study and research in food chemistry, biochemistry, process science, microbiology, safety and toxicology, biotechnology, quality evaluation, and wine biotechnology, ensuring a safe, nutritious, sustainable, and high-quality food supply on a global scale.

The department of Food Material Science offers analytical laboratories and pilot plants for food processing, specializing in material science, structural analysis, and meat technology. Research focuses on creating complex food structures and integrating biologically and physiologically active compounds into food matrices.

The Institute of Food Science and Biotechnology covers Bachelor's, Master's, and Doctoral Studies, news including conferences and colloquia, areas of research and projects, and the institute's twelve departments.

Led by Jean-Paul Vincken, the Food Chemistry Group conducts research and education using analytical and chemical expertise to establish structure-function relationships of food molecules and predictive models. Their work focuses on food proteins, phytochemicals, plant antimicrobials, food lipids, flavour chemistry, carbohydrates, biomass, and enzymology.

The Food Microbiology Group aims to predict and explain microbial behaviour in food, studying fermentation, spoilage, and foodborne diseases. Research themes include food fermentation, quantitative risk assessment, quantitative ecology of pathogens, and physiology and genomics. The group contributes to various bachelor and master programmes.

The University of Guelph Department of Food Science applies chemistry, physics, and microbiology to food processing and product development. It covers undergraduate and graduate programs (including MSc in Food Science), a Food Science Certificate, and continuing education short courses on food safety, production, and science.

The Food Science program focuses on biochemistry, microbiology, safety, processing, engineering, and biotechnology of food systems. Research ensures food security locally, nationally, and internationally by improving availability, wholesomeness, safety, and nutritional quality. Graduates fill industry, government, and academic roles.
